selected_mechanism.texas_consequence: An ERCOT-region AI computing site would need to reconcile its installed-equipment model and field settings with the prior study data before energization. No pending revision is described as currently effective.
selected_mechanism.structural_read: The proposed review makes the study-to-hardware comparison explicit, at the cost of modeling and review work. ERCOT reliability rationale and TIEC scope objections are attributed separately; no preferred policy result is urged.
selected_mechanism.forward_implication: Check PUCT action and effective date first, then as-built review outcome if adopted; avoid treating an attestation or isolated model approval as full permission to energize.

verified_facts.claim: On September 15th, 2026 the ERCOT Board recommended PGRR144 approval. Its status remained pending before PUCT when fetched.
Proposed effective date is the first day of the month after PUCT approval. No date for a PUCT vote appears in the fetched status page or Board Report.
The proposal covers dynamic electrical behavior, including cooling and controls. Large computational load converter models require hardware benchmark validation.

The as-built submission would compare installed settings and model test results with data used in the quarterly stability assessment. ERCOT and the TSP review the effect on the previous stability study.
ERCOT would approve the submission or request more information, with ten Business Days for a response and up to twenty additional Business Days if needed.

Other initial energization conditions include network model inclusion, telemetry, applicable stability and subsynchronous studies and a load commissioning plan. Approval of the model package alone would not authorize energization.
ERCOT describes earlier detection of reliability issues as a benefit. This is ERCOT rationale, not proof of a safety outcome at any named site.
ERCOT forecasts additional review staffing and annual recurring operations and maintenance costs. This supports the post claim about added staff, not a site-specific cost estimate.
TIEC argues that traditional manufacturers often need outside modeling consultants and face additional costs. This is an attributed stakeholder objection to scope beyond computing loads.
The model review applies within the ERCOT system, not every Texas utility territory.
The Board Report records ERCOT staff explaining that PGRR144 addresses a separate issue from Batch Zero. Prior coverage concerned September 9 eligibility RFIs, not as-built electrical model review.

Editorial inference: aligning study and installed-equipment models creates a concrete evidence comparison before energization; a signed attestation enters the review but does not replace ERCOT approval.
Editorial next check: follow the PUCT decision and effective date, then the outcome of as-built review if adopted. No project-level result or public release of protected models is asserted.
